test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Even though ovulation occurs regularly in a female, the uterus lining is shed during menstruation each month. What does this suggest about fertilisation?

options.text: The uterus is rejecting the embryo
The ovary is not releasing eggs

solution:
The correct answer is __**Fertilisation is not occurring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The process of **menstruation** is directly linked to the absence of **fertilisation**. When an **ovum** (egg) is released during **ovulation** and does not meet a **sperm**, the hormonal signals required to maintain the pregnancy environment are not produced. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **uterus lining**, known as the **endometrium**, thickens every month to prepare for the possible implantation of a **fertilised embryo**. If no **embryo** is formed, the **corpus luteum** in the **ovary** stops producing **progesterone**.
 
• The statement "The uterus is rejecting the embryo" is incorrect because, in a normal menstrual cycle where fertilisation does not happen, there is no **embryo** created to be rejected. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
